answer: To deter Sybil attacks, the protocol links equivocation evidence across bonded identities: when k coordinated identities equivocate, aggregate penalties scale as O(k²), rather than as independent linear fines. Detection also triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss, amplified by asymmetric depreciation of escrowed collateral. Thus splitting stake among identities does not dilute risk; a swarm cannot wander free of liability, even when its timber-and-umber identifiers appear unrelated.
